objective: Multiply powers of the same base
constraints: same base; positive integer exponents; add exponents
hints: Keep the common base and multiply the numerical factors.
Add the exponents of that base; treat a bare base as exponent one.
Rewrite with one power and check by expanding a small case.

objective: Numeric bases left in exponent form
constraints: answer stays as a single power, not evaluated
hints: Identify the common numeric base and keep it unchanged.
Add the exponents on the factors with that base.
Write the original base with the combined exponent as one power, and stop without evaluating it.

objective: Three or more factors, including bare bases
constraints: treat a bare base as exponent 1
hints: Separate coefficient multiplication from the repeated variable base.
Add every exponent, including one for a bare variable.
Combine the coefficient and one resulting power.

objective: Divide powers of the same base
constraints: same base; larger exponent on top; subtract exponents
hints: Divide the numerical factor and keep the common variable base.
Subtract the denominator exponent from the numerator exponent.
Check that the remaining exponent is positive.

objective: Numeric bases left in exponent form
constraints: answer stays as a single power, not evaluated
hints: Identify the common nonzero numeric base and keep it unchanged.
Subtract the denominator exponent from the numerator exponent.
Write the original base with the resulting exponent as one power, and stop without evaluating it.

objective: Quotients that leave exponent 1, and bare bases
constraints: treat a bare base as exponent 1; keep results with positive exponents
hints: Treat bare bases as having exponent one before applying the quotient rule.
For matching nonzero bases, subtract the denominator exponent from the numerator exponent.
An exponent of one means write the base once; retain other positive exponents in the simplified result.

objective: Product and quotient rules together
constraints: one product and one quotient step per problem
hints: Combine the product exponents first.
Then subtract the denominator exponent.
Simplify the coefficient separately.

objective: Coefficients with product/quotient rules
constraints: multiply/divide coefficients; apply exponent rule to variables
hints: Multiply and divide coefficients as ordinary numbers.
Add product exponents, then subtract quotient exponents.
Check each part has been simplified.

objective: Two variables at once
constraints: apply the rules base by base
hints: Group factors by each distinct base; do not combine exponents from different bases.
For each base, add numerator exponent contributions and subtract denominator exponent contributions, treating a bare base as exponent one.
Write the simplified factor for every base, then multiply those factors together.

objective: Multiply the exponents
constraints: single variable base; multiply the exponents
hints: Keep the base unchanged.
Multiply the inner and outer exponents.
Apply the resulting exponent to the whole base.

objective: Numeric bases left in exponent form
constraints: answer stays as a single power, not evaluated
hints: Keep the original numeric base unchanged.
Multiply the inner exponent by the outer exponent.
Write the original base with the product exponent as one power, and stop without evaluating it.

objective: Combine with product and quotient rules
constraints: power of a power first, then product/quotient rule
hints: Apply the outer power first by multiplying the inner and outer exponents.
Inspect the remaining same-base operation: add exponents for multiplication or subtract denominator exponents for division.
Write the base with the final exponent and simplify any separate numerical coefficient.

objective: Power of a product
constraints: raise each factor to the power
hints: Raise the coefficient and variable factor separately.
Multiply the variable exponent by the outer exponent.
Write both powered factors together.

objective: Power of a quotient
constraints: raise numerator and denominator to the power
hints: Apply the outer power to both numerator and denominator.
Multiply each inner exponent by it.
Keep the denominator nonzero while simplifying.

objective: Combinations of power rules
constraints: power rules first, then product rule; small coefficients
hints: Apply powers before combining product or quotient factors.
Then combine matching bases with their appropriate rule.
Reduce the numerical coefficient last.

objective: Evaluate a nonzero base to the zero power
constraints: any nonzero base to the 0 power is 1
hints: Rewrite a quotient of equal nonzero powers by subtracting its exponents.
Compare that quotient-rule result with the same nonzero base raised to the resulting exponent.
Use the value required to make the two equivalent expressions agree.

objective: Zero exponents inside expressions
constraints: contrast (ax)^0 with a*x^0
hints: Identify the complete base covered by the zero exponent; parentheses determine whether a whole product or only one factor is powered.
Apply the zero-exponent rule only to that nonzero powered base, leaving every factor outside the exponent in place.
Combine the remaining factors or terms after the powered base has been simplified.

objective: Why it works: the quotient rule
constraints: connect a^0 = 1 to a^n / a^n
hints: Use equal-power cancellation and exponent subtraction to determine the zero exponent case for a nonzero base.
Apply that rule separately to every displayed zero-power term, respecting the grouping of each base.
Perform the remaining addition, subtraction, or multiplication after simplifying the zero powers.

objective: Negative exponent as a reciprocal
constraints: a^-n = 1/a^n
hints: Identify the entire nonzero base carrying the negative exponent.
Invert that base and change the exponent to its positive opposite.
Evaluate a numeric denominator when the base is numeric, or keep a symbolic denominator as a positive power.

objective: Negative exponents in denominators
constraints: a^-n in a denominator moves up as a^n; (a/b)^-1 = b/a
hints: Identify whether the negative exponent applies to a denominator factor or to an entire fraction.
Move a denominator factor with a negative exponent to the numerator with a positive exponent; for a whole fraction raised to negative one, swap numerator and denominator.
Check that the rewritten expression is equivalent on the original nonzero domain and contains only positive exponents.

objective: Combine with exponent rules
constraints: combine exponents first, then rewrite negatives as reciprocals
hints: Combine exponents of the matching base first.
Rewrite any negative resulting exponent as a reciprocal.
Keep the final expression in positive exponents.

objective: Quotients with negative exponents
constraints: subtract exponents carefully with signs; final answer uses positive exponents
hints: Subtract quotient exponents with their signs.
Move a negative resulting power across the fraction bar.
Present the answer using only positive exponents.

objective: Powers of terms with negative exponents
constraints: multiply exponents, keep track of the sign
hints: Multiply the inner and outer exponents, retaining the sign.
Rewrite the negative power as a reciprocal.
Raise the coefficient to the outer power as well.

objective: Full expressions with coefficients and two variables
constraints: coefficients reduce; each variable handled separately
hints: Apply an outside power first when one is present, including to the full numerical coefficient.
Simplify the coefficient ratio and combine exponents separately for each distinct base.
Move every factor with a negative final exponent across the fraction bar, keep original nonzero-domain conditions, and report only positive exponents.
